reasons: Opinion text frames the case around Fourth Amendment privacy, stating that electronic devices capturing conversation are a search within the Amendment.
The opinion states that eavesdropping involves an intrusion on privacy broad in scope, supporting a related cross-doctrine role for reasonable-expectation/privacy materials.
residual_risks: Berger is pre-Katz and should not be used as the source of the Katz reasonable-expectation test itself.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Keep it framed as pre-Katz privacy/electronic-surveillance background.

reasons: The opinion holds that New York's statute was too broad and violative of the Fourth and Fourteenth Amendments.

The opinion states that the Fourth Amendment prescribes a constitutional standard that must be met before official eavesdropping invasion is permissible.
